task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (root-cause diagnosis) for ISS-0816. The issue was filed by ORCH from an unverified CODE-DESIGNER finding: web/src/types/api.ts:17 declares CursorPage<T>.has_more: boolean while Letflow.Api.Pagination.Page emits only {items, next_cursor, count}, and roughly twelve web/ call sites use the shared type without any of them having been audited individually. The substance of this step is that audit. For every CursorPage<T> call site, establish the file and line, the API function, the backend route that function actually calls, and whether that route's response body carries has_more or not; derive the route table by runtime introspection of each router's __authz_routes__/0 plus the mounted forward table rather than by grep, because grep alone misled an earlier run on ISS-0765. Separately establish how many sites READ has_more versus merely being typed with it, since a site that never touches the field is an inert type lie while a site that branches on it is permanently taking the falsy path, and the two need different fixes. Test the issue's own central premise -- that lib/letflow/audit.ex genuinely emits has_more and therefore one shared type is covering two incompatible wire shapes -- against the actual HTTP response builder rather than against the internal function's return value. Also read api.ts:371's pre-existing comment and say what it establishes about how long the gap has been known and which route it names, and confirm or refute AC3's claim that the GroupsPage members dialog reads only the first page and never follows next_cursor, establishing the real default page size from lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex rather than assuming 50 and reading the CURRENT code on main, since .members was retyped to GroupMemberPage by ISS-0765 (merged as dec06da7). Finish with a recommended fix path: one corrected type or a split into two, and which call sites move. Do NOT implement the fix -- route to CODE-DESIGNER per WF-03 Step 2.

summary.headline: ISS-0816's symptom is real and its fix direction is broadly right, but its central premise is FALSE. No backend route in Letflow emits has_more on the wire -- not even the audit route. lib/letflow/audit.ex:276/295-297 is the return shape of the INTERNAL function Letflow.Audit.list_entries/1; lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 consumes that internal has_more, converts it into a next_cursor via next_cursor/2, and serialises an exactly-three-key body {items, next_cursor, count} through page_body/2 at :308-320. has_more never crosses the HTTP boundary. Therefore CursorPage<T> is not one type covering two wire shapes -- it is one type covering ZERO wire shapes for its third field. has_more is 100% client-fabricated wherever it exists at runtime. Consequently the recommended fix is NOT a split into two types (the issue's own suggestion) but the removal of has_more from the single shared type, plus a split along a different axis -- the two-key {items, next_cursor} envelope versus the three-key {items, next_cursor, count} envelope -- which is the real distinction the backend actually makes.

ac2b_audit_premise_refuted.issue_claim: ISS-0816 description: 'has_more IS genuinely emitted by lib/letflow/audit.ex (:276, :295-297), so the field is real for the audit route and absent everywhere Pagination.Page is used. One type covering both cannot be correct for either.'
ac2b_audit_premise_refuted.what_is_actually_at_those_lines: lib/letflow/audit.ex:276 is the @spec of Letflow.Audit.list_entries/1: {:ok, %{items: [Entry.t()], has_more: boolean()}}. :295-297 is its body: {items, has_more} = split_list_page(rows, page_size) ... {:ok, %{items: items, has_more: has_more}}. That is an INTERNAL Elixir map returned to the router, not a JSON body.
ac2b_audit_premise_refuted.what_the_route_actually_sends: lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 -- defp render_page(conn, {:ok, %{items: items, has_more: has_more}}) do / Response.ok(conn, page_body(items, next_cursor(items, has_more))). has_more is consumed as the second argument to the private next_cursor/2 (:292-305), which returns nil when has_more is false and a minted cursor string when it is true. page_body/2 (:308-320) then builds a hand-written three-key map: %{"items" => items, "next_cursor" => next_cursor, "count" => length(items)}. The moduledoc at :308-317 calls it a deliberate INV-2 response allowlist.
ac2b_audit_premise_refuted.verdict: REFUTED. The audit route's wire body is {items, next_cursor, count} -- byte-identical in key set to Pagination.Page's @derive {Jason.Encoder, only: [:items, :next_cursor, :count]} at lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex:81. has_more is strictly internal to the Elixir call. NO route in Letflow emits has_more. Corroborating evidence from the frontend itself: web/src/api/audit.ts:26-40 declares a RawAuditPage of exactly {items, next_cursor, count} -- the client already knows the real shape -- and then FABRICATES the field at :71 with has_more: Boolean(response.next_cursor). web/src/api/promotions.ts:265 does the identical fabrication and its own comment at :249 says so: 'has_more is client-derived -- REQ-397's envelope is exactly {items, next_cursor}'.
ac2b_audit_premise_refuted.consequence_for_the_fix: The issue's proposed split (an audit-shaped type WITH has_more vs a Pagination.Page-shaped type without) would encode a distinction that does not exist. Designing from the issue text alone would have produced a wrong fix. The real axis of variation is two-key vs three-key envelopes.

ac3_who_actually_reads_has_more.consequence: Not one line of production code branches on CursorPage<T>.has_more. Every pagination consumer that exists (AuditLogPage.tsx:81, TenantsPage.tsx:75, DlqPage.tsx:202/203/220, EntityCrudPage.tsx:192/193/197, EntityListBrowserPage.tsx:230/234/237, InstanceBoardPage.tsx:139, InstanceDetailPage.tsx:153/154/369, PromotionReviewListPage.tsx:72) reads next_cursor instead. So has_more is an inert declaration: 13 route-bound call sites are typed with it, 0 read it, and 2 manufacture it locally to satisfy the type they are declared to return. Removing the field breaks no runtime behaviour; it only deletes two now-pointless fabrication lines and their test fixtures. This is what holds the severity at MINOR and it is also what makes the fix cheap.

ac4_api_ts_371_comment.verbatim: /** `POST /entities/query`'s response body. Deliberately NOT `CursorPage<T>`: that shape's `has_more` field does not exist on this route's response (`run_query/4` sends exactly `{"items", "next_cursor"}`) -- reusing `CursorPage<T>` here would silently claim a field the API never sends. */ export interface EntityRecordsPage<T = EntityRecord> { items: T[]; next_cursor: string | null }
ac4_api_ts_371_comment.route_it_concerns: POST /api/v1/entities/query (Letflow.Routers.Entities, {"POST", "/query", :EntitiesQuery}) -- NOT any of the 13 CursorPage<T> call sites. EntityRecordsPage is the escape hatch that route's author built to avoid the bad type.
ac4_api_ts_371_comment.what_it_establishes: The defect was fully understood, correctly diagnosed, and written down in the very file that declares the bad type -- and the bad type was still left in place. The comment names the exact mechanism ('would silently claim a field the API never sends'), so this is not a near-miss observation.
ac4_api_ts_371_comment.how_long_it_has_been_known: At least three independent, dated sightings, all of which chose local avoidance over removal: (1) lib/letflow/design/iss0711-tenant-count-field-mismatch.md:100-104 -- ISS-0711, a BLOCKER fixed on 2026-09-18, whose own design doc states CursorPage<T>'s has_more does not match the real field name; (2) this comment at api.ts:370-373 for EntityRecordsPage; (3) api.ts:474-477, the GroupMemberPage comment -- 'Not CursorPage<T>, which declares a has_more the backend never emits' -- added by ISS-0765 and merged as dec06da7 on 2026-09-25, i.e. the run that then filed ISS-0816. Two further backend-side prose statements exist at lib/letflow/routers/dlq.ex:79 and lib/letflow/routers/services.ex:84. FIVE written acknowledgements, zero removals. This is precisely the process failure ISS-0813 (MAJOR, open) was filed to cover, and it is the strongest argument for fixing the shared type at its source this time rather than adding a sixth local workaround.

ac6_recommended_fix_path.headline: NOT the split ISS-0816 proposes. Delete has_more from the one shared type, then split along the axis the backend actually varies on -- two-key vs three-key envelope.
ac6_recommended_fix_path.why_not_the_issue_s_split: An audit-shaped type carrying has_more and a Pagination-shaped type without it would model a distinction that does not exist on the wire. GET /api/v1/audit's body is {items, next_cursor, count}, key-for-key identical to Pagination.Page's. Building two types on that premise would leave has_more alive on a route that never sends it -- the same defect, relocated.

recommended_shape.step_1: In web/src/types/api.ts, DELETE line 17 (`has_more: boolean`) from CursorPage<T>, leaving { items: T[]; next_cursor: string | null }. This is now the correct, exact type for the six two-key routes: definitions list, definitions search, definitions getVersions, dlq, services (both), promotions.
recommended_shape.step_2: Add a second exported type for the three-key envelope -- suggested name CountedCursorPage<T> = { items: T[]; next_cursor: string | null; count: number } -- and move rows 1 (audit), 6 (instances), 12 and 13 (tasks, both) onto it, along with the derived rows 14 (normalizeTaskPage) and 15 (useAuditLog). GroupMemberPage (api.ts:474-482) is already exactly this shape and should be redefined as CountedCursorPage<GroupMember> rather than left as a fourth hand-rolled duplicate; the same applies to TenantListResponse's envelope from ISS-0711 and to audit.ts's local RawAuditPage (:36-40), both of which are the same three keys written out by hand. CODE-DESIGNER should decide how far to take that consolidation -- it is a simplification, not a requirement of this fix.
recommended_shape.step_3: Delete the two now-unnecessary fabrication lines, audit.ts:71 and promotions.ts:265, and their surrounding .then/mapping where they become identity transforms. auditApi.list still needs its mapAuditEntry mapping; only the has_more key goes.
recommended_shape.step_4: Remove has_more from the four test fixture sites -- DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx:78-80, PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx:119 and :270, TaskInboxPage.test.tsx:134 and :160, web/tests/e2e/obs04.timeline.e2e.spec.ts:72. These fixtures currently assert a wire shape the server does not produce, which is why the whole suite stayed green through five documented sightings of the defect. Leaving them in place would preserve the exact blind spot that let this survive.
recommended_shape.step_5: Fix AC3's real bug independently of the type work: either have groupsApi.members accept cursor/page_size and have GroupsPage follow next_cursor until it is null, or -- the cheaper option -- have the dialog render an explicit truncation notice whenever membersPage.next_cursor is non-null. Following the cursor is preferable; a group over 50 members is not exotic. Either way GroupsPage.tsx must stop treating membersPage.items as the complete set.

ac6_recommended_fix_path.explicitly_out_of_scope_for_this_fix: The two dead modules.ts routes (rows 7 and 8) and definitionsApi.search's ignored limit/offset params are NOT has_more defects and must not be folded into this fix. They are filed separately -- see result.new_findings. Correcting rows 7 and 8's TYPE while their route does not exist would be meaningless work.
ac6_recommended_fix_path.why_tsc_cannot_catch_any_of_this: Every one of these fields is declared required and non-optional on a type applied via a generic client.get<T>() call, which performs no runtime validation. TypeScript checks only that the declared type is used consistently, never that the server honours it. That is the same structural gap named in ISS-0745, ISS-0811, ISS-0814, ISS-0815 and ISS-0813, and no fix confined to web/src/types/api.ts closes it -- only ISS-0813's proposed mechanical coupling to __authz_routes__/0 would.

summary.why_no_existing_test_caught_this: Three reinforcing reasons, all measured. (1) No production code reads has_more, so no assertion could fail on its absence. (2) The four test fixture sites listed above HAND-WRITE has_more into their mock responses, so the tests are asserting against a wire shape that does not exist -- they would pass identically against a server that never sends the field, which is the actual server. (3) There is no contract test, schema check, or generated client coupling web/src/types/api.ts to any router's real response body; that absence is ISS-0813, already filed MAJOR and still open.

finding_1.title: web/src/api/modules.ts targets an entire backend router that does not exist -- the whole process-modules admin surface is non-functional
finding_1.detail: Rows 7 and 8 of the call-site table. modulesApi.list calls GET /api/v1/admin/modules and modulesApi.listShares calls GET /api/v1/admin/module-shares. Neither route is mounted: there is no Letflow.Routers.ProcessModules module in lib/letflow/routers/ and no /admin/modules or /admin/module-shares forward in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:141-200 or lib/letflow/router.ex. lib/letflow/router.ex:82 lists Letflow.Routers.ProcessModules in its 'Deferred routes (not yet mounted -- added by owning stage)' table against stage S5. The surface is larger than those two functions: modulesApi.get, .register, .publish, .grantShare and .revokeShare all target the same non-existent prefixes, and web/src/hooks/useModules.ts plus web/src/pages/admin/modules/ProcessModulesPage.tsx are built on top of all of them. This is the same defect class as ISS-0765 (MAJOR) but wider -- ISS-0765 was a wrong prefix on an existing router; this is a frontend screen shipped against a backend that was never built. Recommend ORCH file it via register_task. NOT folded into ISS-0816: fixing a has_more declaration on a function that 404s would be meaningless.

finding_2.title: Four test fixture sites hand-write has_more into mock API responses, so the suite would pass identically against a server that never sends it -- the blind spot that kept this defect alive through five documented sightings
finding_2.detail: web/src/pages/dlq/__tests__/DlqPage.pagination.test.tsx:77-80 types its fixture map as Record<string, CursorPage<DlqEntry>> and writes has_more: true/true/false across three pages; PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx:119 and :270, TaskInboxPage.test.tsx:134 and :160, and web/tests/e2e/obs04.timeline.e2e.spec.ts:72 do the same with has_more: false. GET /api/v1/dlq's body is documented at lib/letflow/routers/dlq.ex:79 as 'an exactly-two-key map, {"items", "next_cursor"} -- no has_more'. A fixture that fabricates a field the server does not send cannot fail when the server does not send it, which is the general mechanism, not a detail of this one field: the same pattern would mask ISS-0745, ISS-0811, ISS-0814 and ISS-0815 equally well. Worth filing as its own testing-practice issue (fixtures for a wire shape must be derived from that route's real response builder) rather than being silently cleaned up inside ISS-0816's fix, because the practice outlives this field. The fixture edits themselves ARE in scope for ISS-0816's fix -- see ac6_recommended_fix_path.step_4.

finding_3.title: definitionsApi.search sends dead limit/offset query params the backend ignores -- the same params ISS-0711 removed from tenants.ts
finding_3.detail: web/src/api/definitions.ts:49-51 declares search: (params: { q: string; limit?: number; offset?: number }) and forwards them as query params. lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex:519-534's handle_search/1 reads exactly three params -- q, cursor, page_size -- and validates page_size through Pagination. limit and offset are silently dropped, so a caller passing offset gets page one every time. web/src/hooks/useDefinitions.ts:94 is a live caller passing both. This is the request-side twin of the response-side defect ISS-0711 fixed, and it is not a has_more problem, so it is filed rather than folded in.

notes: Step 1's 'reproduce directly' obligation was met statically rather than by an HTTP call, and deliberately so. The property under diagnosis is 'does this JSON body contain the key has_more', and every list route in scope builds its body from a hand-written, closed map literal or from Pagination.Page's @derive allowlist -- both of which are complete, quotable specifications of the key set. There is no dynamic path, no conditional key insertion, and no merge that could add a key at runtime. A live curl would confirm the same key set the source already fixes, and would additionally require a provisioned tenant and token per route across ten routes. The one claim that genuinely could not be settled from a type declaration -- whether the audit route's internal has_more survives to the wire -- was settled by reading the actual call chain render_page/2 -> next_cursor/2 -> page_body/2 end to end, which is where the issue's own premise fails.
